source_snapshot.procedure_direct_xlsx: 【Before Test】 1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition. 2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.). 【During Test】 Hardware required: RDIMM with ECC / HDT Software tool: AMD RAS Error Injection Tool 1. BIOS settings: a. CPU Common Options → Platform First Error Handling: Enabled b. CPU Common Options → MCA error thresh enable: TRUE c. CPU Common Options → MCA error thresh count: FFE (Deviate from default setting FF5) d. UMC Common Options → DDR RAS → RCD Parity: Enabled e. UMC Common Options → DDR RAS → Disable Memory Error Injection: False f. FCH Common Options → FCH RAS Options → Reset After Sync-Flood: Enabled 2. Unlock CPU via HDT. 3. Boot into Ubuntu 20.04/RHEL 9.0 / Windows 2022. 4. Download the AMD RAS Error Injection Tool, then install and open the software. 5. Enter the following commands: sudo ./cmdline_amdraserrorinjectiontest –-listvalidumc 6. Correctable Error Injection, enter the following commands: sudo ./cmdline_amdraserrorinjectiontest --dramothererrors --errortype 0 --socketdieumc 0:0:3 --enablemcapolling 0 --errormode 1 【After Test】 1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders. 2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria_direct_xlsx: 1. For correctable errors, the tool provides a PASS status. 2. For uncorrectable errors, verify that the errors are logged correctly in BERT dmesg after the warm reset is triggered. 3. If the OS reports the error within a timeout period, the test passed. 4. If the OS does not report the error within a timeout period, the test failed.
source_snapshot.deepseek_direct_xlsx: PARTIAL | -- Memory slot 1~N: inject the DRAM parity correctable error on Memory slot 1~N via the AMD RAS Error Injection Tool (after HDT/unlock + the BIOS RAS knobs from the procedure, e.g. Platform First Error Handling=Enabled + per-unit MCA/UMC settings). Agent stages/verifies with sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "dmesg -T 2>&1 | tail -160 | grep -iE 'corrected|uncorrected|mce|EDAC|umc|address.error|parity'; echo __DRAM_parity_correctable_error_on_Memory_slot_1~N; ipmitool sel elist 2>&1 | tail -40 2>&1" but the tool injection step itself is interactive/HW-level and needs the user to drive the exact inject command.
